newsitem.title: THAILAND: Finance One says in debt repayment talks.
newsitem.headline: Finance One says in debt repayment talks.

text.p: Ailing Thai finance firm Finance One Plc is in talks with foreign creditors to discuss repayment of debts worth approximately $46.4 million, the company said in a statement on Wednesday.
Finance One, formerly the country's largest non-bank financial institution, is facing an uncertain future following the collapse of a celebrated merger.

Finance One announced plans to merge with medium-sized Thai Danu Bank Plc at the end of February, in a move viewed by some industry executives as necessary to avoid an impending liquidity crunch at the troubled firm.
But the merger, a major test of government policy to encourage consolidation to bolster systemic stability in the troubled Thai finance sector, collapsed in May.
The firms cited economic and legal difficulties for the break up, though some analysts pointed to the dubious quality of Finance One's loan book as a major factor in the split.
Many Thai finance firms are struggling to cope with high funding costs and declining asset quality as the country goes through its toughest economic test for more than a decade.
A senior local executive said on Monday that Thai finance firms may have non-performing loans averaging 31.5 percent of total lending.
Following the merger collapse, Finance One President Pin Chakkapak announced plans to recapitalise and restructure his firm and apply for a banking licence.
The recapitalisation process is currently underway in the form of a large share issue.
In the statement Pin said investors would be informed of any progress made from creditor talks.
